title: The Price of One Metro Stop in Paris
dek: Mapping 173,877 official French property deeds around 316 metro stations uncovers single-stop €4,341/m² cliffs—and a striking inversion where central Paris studios trade up to 30.4% cheaper per square meter than family apartments.
byline: Data Visual Essay · Geo-DVF (2023–2025) & Île-de-France Mobilités

parisContext.rentControlNote: 2025 Paris Encadrement des loyers: 1-room reference rent (€30.50/m²) stays +20.3% to +41.5% above 4-room (€23.80/m²) in every neighborhood—proving the central purchase flip is driven by Haussmannian trophy scarcity vs. 6th-floor chambres de bonne.

beats.headline: One €2.50 metro ticket spans a 5.7× housing divide

at Rosny–Bois-Perrier—a 5.7× gap. Yet prices do not fade smoothly outward; they fracture at sharp single-stop cliffs.

beats.takeaway: 173,877 clean DVF sales (2023–2025) across 316 stops: €16,500/m² peak vs €2,920/m² floor.

beats.headline: In central Paris, the studio penalty completely flips sign

bodySegments.text: Lore says studios (<25m²) always cost more per m² than large flats (>70m²). Across 291 paired stations (r = −0.80), that rule breaks at €9,890/m². Below €7k/m², studios carry a
to a 12.4% median studio discount (21.8% above €14k/m²).

beats.takeaway: r = −0.80: studios cost +15.1% more in outer stops, but 12.4% less in all 49/49 prime stops.

beats.headline: Regulated rents penalize studios; buyers pay for trophy space

bodySegments.text: Paris's 2025 rent-control schedule still sets 1-room ceilings at least +20.3% higher per m² (up to +41.5% citywide) than 4-room flats. Yet at Rue du Bac,
attic chambres de bonne (−30.4%), while outer stops like Porte d'Ivry (+44.4%) preserve the studio yield.

beats.takeaway: Paris regulated rents stay +20.3% to +41.5% higher for studios even where sale prices flip −30.4%.
